rationale:
Evidence: iteration 1 is the best raced design (score 134.06). It finished once in 20 oval trials and left the track in all other trials, with progress about 0.50 on the oval, 0.28 on the s-bend and 0.14 on the slalom. Line-loss events ran at 1.15 to 1.45 per run and steering_oscillation reached 0.29 on the oval. Every failure is an off-track exit at max_error about 0.06 m (the limit), so the tape is slipping past the 5-sensor array at bends. Iterations 2 and 3 were never raced, so their ideas are untested. Iteration 2 used base_speed 1.1, which is too slow for the 3 s limit (about 1.5 m/s average needed). I am therefore carrying forward iteration 3's plan, with one correction.

Changes: (1) Widen the array to x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 m and use 16 mm footprints. The 0.02 m spacing with 16 mm footprints means the 25 mm tape always overlaps at least one sensor, which should cut line-loss events toward 0.5 per run. (2) Keep base_speed at 1.4, the level that produced the only oval finish. (3) Raise kp from 3.0 to 3.7. The wider spacing lowers the signal per metre of tape offset (about 50 per m instead of about 67 per m), so this keeps the effective steering gain near 185 versus 200 before, instead of the 3.5 I planned earlier. (4) Raise kd from 0.4 to 0.5 to damp the oval oscillation. (5) Keep ki at 0.02 to avoid windup, keep mass 0.6 kg, keep sensor y at 0.03 m and keep last_direction line loss so that only the array width, kp and kd move.

Expected result: line_loss_events at or below 0.5 per run, fewer off-track exits, and progress above 0.4 on the s-bend and slalom with more oval completions.

Hypotheses to test: (a) if line-loss events stay above 0.8 with the wider array, turn-in lag is the cause, so kd or sensor y must change next; (b) if max_error reaches 0.06 on the s-bend with no line loss, kp is too low for the sharp bends; (c) if the robot is steady but progress is under 0.5 at the 3 s cap, base_speed must rise toward 1.6 with kd holding the line.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort, so the array width, gain and damping effects can be separated.
